headline: Nasdaq-100 closes the payroll session higher after a full two-way range; low VIX and orderly yields keep Tail low into the pre-holiday futures settlement
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,544.15, up 0.21% against a 29,482.32 prior close, after opening at 29,539.57, extending to 29,655.22, fully retracing that advance to a 29,440.15 low and then recovering into the close. Retracements occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure this Tail score measures. Volatility confirms the reading: VIX finished at 14.54, up 1.54% but historically low, inside a 13.80-14.58 range. The August employment report printed 162,000 payrolls against roughly 55,000 expected, with unemployment steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% year-on-year, moving September Fed hike pricing into the 58-60% area ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC. Rate transmission stayed orderly rather than disorderly: the 10-year closed at 4.784%, up about 2 basis points inside a 4.748-4.812 range, with the 2-year in the 4.3-4.4% area. Index internals were unusually split rather than aligned, which argues against a single directional impulse: semiconductors were firm, with Micron up 4.24%, AMD up 3.66% and Arm up 3.20%, while Apple fell 2.17%, Microsoft 1.80%, Alphabet 1.19% and Tesla 6.40%. The broader tape diverged from the Nasdaq-100, with the Nasdaq Composite down 0.29% and the S&P 500 down 0.38%. Energy remains the most active cross-asset carry: Brent is near $95.9 and WTI near $91.2, up roughly 6-8% on the week, as US-Iran hostilities entered their seventh month and Strait of Hormuz transits fell to four vessels on Thursday against a 10-day average near 15. That combination supports elevated Stress without the aligned one-way price path that would lift Tail. Cash equities are now closed and CME equity index futures settle at 21:00 UTC, after which the horizon contains no live price path until the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours cover a calm overnight regime, the August payroll release and its decay into the cash close. Tail drifted between 12% and 17% through the Asian and European sessions while Stress climbed steadily into the print. The 12:00 UTC hour carried the only genuine spike, with Tail at 24%, Stress at 76% and Confidence down to 74% as event/whipsaw mode took over. Price discovery then proved orderly: Tail decayed through 20%, 18%, 17%, 15%, 14% and 13% over the following hourly assessments as retracements appeared in both directions and volatility fell, and the mode reverted to mixed. No hour in the window required a blocking action.
outlookSummary: The current post-close hour keeps two-sided structure with Tail at 12% inside the flagged 20:00-21:00 UTC window, which covers thin futures trade into the CME equity index settlement at 21:00 UTC. From that settlement the entire remainder of this horizon is a halted market with no live price path, so forecast Tail falls to a 4-6% closed-venue floor and the published dominant mode of normal denotes a closed venue rather than a resolved regime. Residual Stress in the 36-40% band carries what cannot price until the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen, principally unresolved US-Iran hostilities with Brent near $96, and secondarily September Fed hike pricing near 58-60% into the 15-16 September FOMC. Monday 7 September is the Labor Day holiday, so the next US cash session is Tuesday 8 September and the next scheduled US macro checkpoints are PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September.
